sources.note: Generalizes causal tracing from one component or layer at a time to selecting subsets of components jointly, by relaxing the combinatorial search into a continuous one over soft interventions.
sources.title: Multi-component Causal Tracing in Large Language Models

sources.note: Explains LLM counting failures as a depth limit, since counting is computed across layers, and fixes it with a System-2 decomposition whose mechanism is then traced.
sources.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Large-Scale Counting in LLMs through a System-2 Strategy

sources.note: Systematically varies the methodological choices in activation patching — how prompts are corrupted, which metric scores the patching effect, and whether layers are patched singly or in sliding windows — and shows each choice can change which model components a study concludes are important.
sources.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods

sources.note: Uses causal mediation analysis on a minimal propositional logic task to recover a sparse reasoning circuit in Mistral-7B and Gemma-2 up to 27B, and decomposes it into four families of attention heads that execute rule locating, rule moving, fact processing and decision making as sequential steps.
sources.title: A Implies B: Circuit Analysis in LLMs for Propositional Logical Reasoning

sources.note: Trains sparse autoencoders on language model activations to recover an overcomplete dictionary of sparsely activating directions, and shows those directions are more interpretable and more precisely causal than neurons, PCA or ICA.
sources.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models

result.definition: Measuring a component's causal contribution to an outcome by intervening on it while holding the rest of the computation fixed — the framework activation patching instantiates. The archived sources have moved from citing it as lineage to working with it. Two use it as the method proper: one recovers a sparse propositional-logic circuit in models up to 27B and decomposes it into four families of attention heads whose roles are verified by targeted counterfactual patching, and one traces the mechanism behind a System-2 decomposition of counting. One generalizes the technique, relaxing the combinatorial search over which components to intervene on into a continuous one over soft interventions so subsets can be chosen jointly rather than one component or layer at a time. One is a methodological audit finding that the choices inside a patching experiment — how the prompt is corrupted, which metric scores the effect, whether layers are patched singly or in sliding windows — each change the conclusion. None works with the formal decomposition of counterfactual effects into direct and indirect parts.
